claims.statement: Image segmentation lacks a foundation model capable of zero-shot transfer to new distributions and tasks.
Segmentation masks are not naturally abundant on the internet, preventing the standard web-scale data collection strategy used for NLP foundation models.
The research question is whether a promptable segmentation task, a capable model, and sufficient training data can together enable zero-shot generalization across segmentation tasks.
SAM consists of an image encoder (MAE pre-trained ViT-H), a prompt encoder (handling points, boxes, masks, and text), and a lightweight mask decoder that together allow amortized real-time prompting.
The three-stage data engine (assisted-manual, semi-automatic, fully automatic) was necessary to collect SA-1B.
SA-1B contains 1.1 billion masks from 11 million licensed, privacy-respecting images — 400x more masks than any prior segmentation dataset.

In zero-shot single-point evaluation across 23 diverse datasets, SAM outperforms RITM (strongest interactive segmentation baseline) on 16 of 23 datasets by automatic mIoU; with oracle ambiguity resolution, outperforms RITM on all 23.
Human raters consistently score SAM's masks substantially higher than RITM's (mean ratings 7-9 on 1-10 scale) in a blinded study across 7 diverse datasets.

In zero-shot instance segmentation, SAM achieves AP 46.5 on COCO and 44.7 on LVIS, trailing fully supervised ViTDet-H (51.0, 46.6) on automatic metrics but achieving higher human-rated mask quality (8.1 vs 7.9).
In zero-shot edge detection on BSDS500, SAM achieves ODS=.768 without training on BSDS500, competitive with the 2015 supervised HED (ODS=.788) though below the 2022 state of the art.
SAM's promptable interface enables composable use as a segmentation module in larger systems without per-task retraining.
SAM misses fine structures, hallucinates small disconnected components, and is not real-time when the heavy image encoder is included.
Automatically generated SA-1B masks achieve 94% >90% IoU agreement with professional annotators, comparable to or exceeding inter-annotator consistency (85-91% IoU) from prior work.
Training SAM on only automatically generated masks (vs. all data engine stages) reduces mIoU by only ~0.5; 1M images gives comparable results to full 11M images.

SAM shows no statistically significant performance difference across perceived gender presentation or skin tone for people segmentation; a bias is detected for clothing segmentation across perceived gender.

limitations.statement: SAM not real-time when heavy image encoder included
Text-to-mask is a proof of concept, not fully robust
All evaluations are zero-shot; fine-tuned domain-specific tools likely outperform SAM in their domains
Geographic dataset coverage underrepresents Africa and low-income countries
Bias detected in clothing segmentation across perceived gender; SAM users should be mindful when used in larger systems
